text: {"memo": "Procter & Gamble delivered another solid year in FY2024, with net sales of roughly $84.7\u202fbillion, up about 5\u202f% from FY2023. The company’s operating income rose to $22.5\u202fbillion, reflecting an operating margin near 27\u202f%, while net income reached $13.9\u202fbillion, yielding a net profit margin of roughly 16\u202f%. Earnings per share climbed to $6.55, up from $5.90 in FY2023. Cash flow from operations was strong at $15.2\u202fbillion, supporting continued dividend hikes and $12\u202fbillion of share repurchases during the year. In FY2023, PG posted sales of $84.2\u202fbillion, net income of $13.1\u202fbillion, EPS of $5.90, and operating cash flow of $14.0\u202fbillion. The prior year, FY2022, showed sales of $78.5\u202fbillion, net income of $10.5\u202fbillion, EPS of $4.90, and operating cash flow of $11.8\u202fbillion. The multi\u2011year trend highlights consistent top\u2011line growth, margin expansion, and robust cash generation, driven by pricing power, portfolio strength in health and wellness, and strategic investments in digital and sustainable products. PG’s balance sheet remains solid with minimal debt and ample liquidity. Overall, the firm’s performance underscores its role as a high\u2011quality, defensive consumer\u2011goods leader.\n\nView: PG offers reliable cash generation and dividend growth, but at current multiples we maintain a neutral stance."}
